note: Approved real estate of US$750,000. The regulation gives this for 'up to a family of four', and no lower figure exists for a single applicant. On paper the Capital Development Fund route is cheaper (US$150,000 single, t-76e5e3d790), but in December 2022 the Executive Council recorded that it 'was not available ... because the fund was not established' (e-880c0f7f74). The 2024 amending Act and Regulations were not retrieved, so it is unknown whether the fund route works today. If it does, the headline should become US$150,000 (donation). Fees excluded: permit fee US$10,000 and due diligence.
No price: citizenship is by nomination only, and nobody can apply or buy it (programme notes).

Property worth at least AED 2 million (10-year golden residence, Res. 65/2022, in force 3 Oct 2022; Dubai and Abu Dhabi pages agree). The same AED 2 million applies to a bank deposit or a company share (t-9712802f47, t-accf082b73). Mortgaged or off-plan property counts if AED 2 million has been paid. Government fees excluded (about AED 9,885 in Dubai).
No amount: the Ministry of Economy has not published what counts as a 'relevant investment' (no resolution found up to 1 Oct 2026). There are no term rows.

ARS 1,500,000 productive, commercial or service investment, fixed in nominal pesos in 2010 (Decree 616/2010); no later update found. After years of inflation it is worth very little in other currencies, so the figure may be out of date in practice.

National Development Fund contribution of US$230,000 for a single applicant or a family (2024 regulations, from 1 Aug 2024; the CIU page still gives it in Sep 2026). Alternatives: real estate US$300,000 (t-9f8da8a4d9), UWI Fund US$260,000 (t-3f8135c77e, for a family of at least six; the CIU says it includes fees), business US$1.5m (t-b589105440). Fees excluded: processing US$10,000, due diligence US$8,500.

On closure (31 Jul 2024 per the visa website, 1 Jul 2024 per the Migration Program report), the Investor stream required an AUD 2.5 million complying investment for those invited on or after 1 July 2021, family included. Other BIIP streams (business innovation, entrepreneur) had no fixed investment. The Significant Investor stream (AUD 5m) is recorded separately as aus-siv.
No term rows: the programme notes say the investment thresholds over time have not been sourced.
Complying premium investment of at least AUD 15 million, by Austrade invitation only. This was the rule when the stream closed (applications up to 30 Jun 2021).
Complying significant investment of at least AUD 5 million (20/30/50 split from 1 July 2021), family included. This was the rule when the stream closed on 31 Jul 2024.
No price: discretionary naturalisation for 'extraordinary achievements', with no published investment amount.

The cheapest route was the ordinary art. 12a route: about EUR 500,000 (in law BGN 1 million), then 5 years of investor permanent residence. The source is the Commission's 2019 description (t-de2b625424). Most actual grants (46 of 50 in 2013-Jan 2019) used the art. 14a fast track, which required the investment to be raised to BGN 2 million (about EUR 1m; t-9673f014e5, t-7f8c9280f1). From 2021 there was also BGN 1 million in a priority-project company with a 1-year wait (t-c92ed66ac3). All routes were repealed 1 Apr 2022.

BGN 1,000,000 in concession rights (the most used route), Bulgarian collective investment schemes or Bulgarian AIFs (items 6(b)-(d), consolidated text as at 2 Oct 2026). Other routes: BGN 2m in listed securities or a priority project; BGN 6m in an unlisted company.

Property worth at least BHD 130,000 (cut from BHD 200,000 on 26 Nov 2025, per an NPRA press release; the legal instrument was not found). Property is the only investment route. Fees excluded: BHD 300 per person, BHD 5 application.

BS$1 million in real estate or Central Bank zero-coupon bonds (or a mix), held 10 years. The rule has applied since 1 Jan 2025. The statute says only 'dollars' (Bahamian dollars, at par with US$). Fees excluded: BS$20,000-25,000 certificate fee.

Weak evidence. The US State Department reported two buyers paying '$25,000 apiece' in December 2001, shortly before sales ended in January 2002. No official price schedule was found, and the currency is not stated (presumably US$). Consider leaving it empty if only official schedules are wanted.

BD$2.5 million in any qualifying investment (real estate, business, charity, Sinking Fund, Trust Fund), with spouse and dependants included. The government-bond option was removed on 9 June 2024. Fees excluded: BD$2,625 certificate fee.

R$500,000 of the applicant's own foreign funds invested in a Brazilian company (RN 118/2015, kept by RN 13/2017). The real-estate route needs R$1,000,000, or R$700,000 in the North and Northeast (RN 36/2018, later RN 46). A lower amount for innovation projects is reported by law firms but was not confirmed.

Not determinable from official sources. The only amount (US$2m investment plus US$5m net worth, Category 1) comes from a business magazine, and the notes mention a cheaper Category 2 (US$300,000 real estate) with no term row. No official text with thresholds was found.

C$800,000 interest-free loan to the federal government, repaid after 5 years (net worth C$1.6m; family included). These were the terms from 1 Dec 2010 until the law ended the programme on 19 Jun 2014. Intake had already stopped on 1 Jul 2012. It is a refundable loan, not a payment; most investors financed it through banks.
C$2,000,000 into a venture capital fund, repayment not guaranteed (net worth C$10m). Intake ran 28 Jan-30 Dec 2015.

Since 1 Jan 2024 both are required: a C$1,000,000 five-year placement with IQ Immigrants Investisseurs, refundable without interest (t-f7f008961c), plus a non-refundable C$200,000 contribution (t-34bd71f90b). The total outlay is C$1.2m. Before 2024 it was a C$1.2m placement alone (t-e5d8f200e2).

No investment price: this is a tax regime. The federal minimum taxable expenditure base is CHF 435,000 from 2026 (t-a336fd097b), but that is a tax base, not an amount invested or donated, and cantons set their own minimums.
No federal amount: each canton sets its own minimum tax expectation. There are no term rows.

Weak evidence. The IMF says citizenship was granted 'in exchange for KMF 1 million; about US$3,000' per person. This looks like the official fee rather than what buyers paid. Most sales were bulk deals with the UAE (EUR 4,600 per passport under the 2011 agreement, t-1dad1be5d1). The parliamentary report puts individual prices at EUR 25,000-200,000 (t-8757c1f6aa). Sales were suspended in May 2016.
Property of at least EUR 80,000 in a municipality with below-average GDP per capita; EUR 120,000 elsewhere (t-8be2cdd4d6). Paid with money transferred from abroad.
No price: the law that would set the investment amounts has not been passed (programme notes).

US$150,000 under Ley 9996, in force 14 Jul 2021. Caveat: the law sets this amount 'for the period set by this law', and its benefits ran only five years (to about July 2026). It is unresolved whether the minimum has gone back to US$200,000 (t-39ca44e5c4) since then. Investment can be in real estate, shares, securities, productive projects and other assets.
CI$1 million in an employment-generating business that the holder manages. Fees excluded: CI$20,000 issue fee.
CI$2 million in developed real estate (since 26 May 2017; still the prescribed sum). Fees excluded: CI$100,000 issue fee (draft CI$200,000).

CI$1 million on Grand Cayman, of which at least CI$500,000 must be in developed real estate. The applicant also needs CI$120,000 annual income or a CI$400,000 deposit. Regional discount: CI$500,000 on Cayman Brac or Little Cayman (CI$250,000 real estate), noted in the same row. Fees excluded: CI$20,000.
No minimum investment: the requirement is a qualifying business with premises and four resident staff. Only the CI$5,000 issue fee is fixed.

At closure (regulations ΚΔΠ 379/2020, applications up to 31 Oct 2020) the applicant needed all three: an investment of at least EUR 2,000,000 (t-e5a592f8b1), two donations of EUR 100,000 each (t-ab40ed5f97, t-06b47e9e39), and a permanent home in Cyprus worth at least EUR 500,000 plus VAT (t-92d5cbff51). The EUR 2.2m assumes the home can be part of a real-estate investment, as earlier decisions allowed (t-2344c31f0c note). If it cannot, the total is about EUR 2.7m plus VAT. The Audit Office says applicants who filed before 18 Aug 2020 were treated under the 2019 rules (EUR 2m plus EUR 150,000 in donations). Fees excluded: EUR 7,000.

EUR 300,000. For a new home bought from a developer this is plus VAT; the same EUR 300,000 applies to company share capital, Cypriot fund units and commercial property (criteria in force 2 May 2023). The applicant must also show EUR 50,000 a year of income (t-9741560c6c), which is not an investment.

Economic Diversification Fund contribution of US$200,000 for a main applicant (S.R.O. 8 of 2024, from 28 Jun 2024; confirmed by the CBIU brochure). The real-estate route is also US$200,000 (t-0c2ddb08dd), but it adds a US$75,000 government fee. Fees excluded.
Not determinable: the minimum amount has not been confirmed. The migration director cited US$250,000 in 2021, and advisers cite US$200,000. There are no term rows.

Non-refundable USD 250,000 paid to the Treasury (PM Decree 876/2023, in force 3 Mar 2023; instalments over a year allowed). Alternatives: property USD 300,000 (t-9ddc766426), a refundable USD 500,000 deposit (t-59d92cd291), or a USD 350,000 project plus USD 100,000 to the Treasury. Fees excluded: USD 10,000 application fee.
Bank deposit of at least EGP 7 million under Law 173/2018. After 5 years the deposit passed to the Treasury on naturalisation. Repealed by Law 140/2019; no permit is known to have been issued.

Property of at least EUR 500,000 per applicant, free of charges (art. 64 b) Ley 14/2013). This was the rule until the route was abolished (last day 2 Apr 2025). Alternatives: EUR 1m in shares, deposits or funds; EUR 2m in public debt.

The cheapest route is EUR 16,000 of capital invested by a sole proprietor (enterprise permit). That is an entrepreneur permit and requires running the business. A company shareholder needs EUR 65,000 (t-d58fbc6b83). The passive large-investor permit, the closest to a 'golden visa', needs EUR 1,000,000 (t-e74d31e3a1, from 18 Jan 2017). The main session may prefer the EUR 1m figure for comparability.
Economic investment of at least EUR 300,000 in France that creates or saves jobs within four years (current ANEF checklist).
GBP 2 million invested in UK companies' share or loan capital. Government bonds were excluded from 29 Mar 2019. This was the rule when the route closed on 17 Feb 2022.

A single property of at least 120 m2 worth EUR 400,000 outside the high-demand areas (Law 5100/2024, for deposits after 31 Aug 2024). The figure is EUR 800,000 in Attica, Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini and larger islands (t-75612cd3c5). Niche routes cost EUR 250,000 anywhere: commercial-to-residential conversions and listed buildings (t-a4e6f5b664, t-3d28093051). Financial investment permits (type B.4) are a separate permit type: EUR 350,000 in funds (t-646e3c9019), EUR 500,000 in deposits or bonds.

National Transformation Fund contribution from 1 Jul 2024; the same amount covers a main applicant with up to 3 dependants, so a single applicant pays it too. Real-estate alternatives cost more: US$270,000 share in an approved unit (t-9682e1c20a) or US$350,000 whole investment (t-31e639c14c), each plus a US$50,000 government contribution (t-e32287fd40). Older rows t-d2fbafe7c0 (US$200,000) and t-3c00a0005e (US$150,000, to 30 Jun 2024) are superseded.

Price on closure (suspended Nov 2001). Rests only on an industry blog ('The prices for Grenada passport was only $39,000 going back to 1997'), which puts the total including fees at $50,000; unverified, and who it covered is not stated. Treat as low reliability.
Threshold on the day the scheme was suspended (15 Jan 2015): HK$10m in permissible financial assets; real estate no longer counted after 14 Oct 2010. Covers spouse and minor children.
HK$30m in total: at least HK$27m in permissible assets (real estate counts for at most HK$10m) plus HK$3m in the CIES Investment Portfolio. Applicant also needs HK$30m net assets.

Not a passive investment: the applicant must own at least 51% of a company or craft, invest at least EUR 26,544.56 in founding it and employ three Croatian citizens full-time. Start date of the euro amount not checked.

Units of a qualified Hungarian real estate fund, held 5 years. Alternatives: EUR 1,000,000 donation to a foundation-run university (t-0acf83b0be); the EUR 500,000 property route (t-bfb4bb20e7) was removed from 30 Dec 2024 and seems never to have operated.

Price at closure (31 Mar 2017): EUR 300,000 face value of residency bonds per applicant, for applications filed after 1 Jan 2015 (EUR 250,000 before, t-36b425f7c7). Intermediaries' service fees (reported EUR 45,000-60,000) excluded.

Individual investor not founding a company, 5-year permit: US$350,000 in Indonesian government bonds, listed shares or deposits. 10-year permit US$700,000 (t-64b3f7d8b6); founding a company US$2.5m. Thresholds as stated by Immigration in Feb 2026; the regulation itself was not read.

Rule in force when the scheme ended: a net investment of at least IR£1 million per applicant (from Oct 1994), held 5 years, plus a residence in Ireland. New applications stopped 4 Sep 1996; formal end 20 Apr 1998.

At closure (15 Feb 2023) the cheapest route was a EUR 500,000 philanthropic endowment by one individual. EUR 400,000 each where 5 or more investors pool for one project (t-77f124e2e0). Investment routes cost EUR 1m (enterprise t-12eb30ac09, approved fund t-0ec540d544) or EUR 2m (REIT); most investors used the enterprise route. Investors also needed EUR 2m net worth.

Cheapest route: EUR 250,000 in an Italian innovative start-up, held 2 years. Others: EUR 500,000 in an Italian company or venture-capital fund (t-3b80f5d965), EUR 1m donation (t-66ee841f28), EUR 2m government bonds (t-83df76feae). Applicant must also show EUR 1m available funds (EUR 2m for bonds).

Rules from 2 Jul 2025 (decision 4375): new project outside Amman with at least JOD 500,000 invested and 10 Jordanian jobs; first a 3-year temporary passport, citizenship after 3 years of compliance. The passive route is JOD 1m in new shares held 3 years (t-bb292d0da6); a new project in Amman needs JOD 700,000 (t-bcdb28d059). Lower thresholds for investors with existing projects (JOD 350,000 outside Amman, t-0822b326c4) were not chosen because they apply only to investments already held for 3 years. Amounts in JOD from 2025 (USD before).
New residential property bought from a licensed developer, held 5 years; spouse and children included.

Sub-decree 225 (from 1 Dec 2025): own capital of at least 4 billion riel spent on a project in a priority sector listed in the annexes; donation route 12 billion riel (t-a5a25d1684). Also 12 months' legal residence for investors (2018 law). Amounts for 2018-2025 (sub-decree 112) not found.

Sustainable Island State Contribution from 8 Jul 2024: US$250,000 for a main applicant or a family of up to four; still listed on 28 Sep 2026. Public benefit option also US$250,000 (t-69fe4cd14c); approved real estate US$325,000 (t-fb847390c5). The CIU announced a move away from contribution routes during 2026 (e-ff2a74727e); no new rule recorded yet. Several undated older rows (SIDF, SGF, US$400,000 real estate) need end dates (see contradictions).
General public-project fund route from 29 Jun 2023 (F-2, then F-5 after 5 years); immediate F-5 route 3bn won (t-04e78a8eb5). Principal returned without interest after five years.

Tourism/resort property in the five designated areas from 1 May 2023. The designation was extended by three years from May 2023 (to about April 2026); whether it was extended again was not checked, so 'today' may not hold.

National Economic Fund from 1 Jul 2024; the amount covers an applicant with up to three dependants, so a single applicant pays the same. Alternatives: enterprise Option 3 US$250,000 (t-df72f95314), real estate US$300,000 (t-1125ad0c7c), National Action Bond US$300,000 (t-19c9485fef).

Not a passive investment: EUR 14,000 of own money in a Lithuanian company with at least EUR 28,000 equity, active 6 months, paying staff at least twice the average wage, applicant manager or holding a third of shares. Alternative EUR 260,000 with five jobs (t-6a1b173be9). Start date of the amounts not established.
EUR 500,000 in an existing (held 5 years) or new (held 3 years) Luxembourg company. Alternatives EUR 3m in an investment structure, EUR 20m deposit. Repeal bill 8586 pending in Sep 2026.

Under the new Immigration Law from 15 Sep 2026 only the business route remains usable: EUR 50,000 in a company with up to 50 employees (2-year permit), plus a EUR 10,000 state payment (a fee, t-8b87d829d3). The new EUR 150,000 state-fund route (t-2cd2f2a778) was not yet operational. The EUR 250,000 property and EUR 280,000 bank routes ended 14 Sep 2026; the state-securities route ended 19 May 2026.
No program_terms rows: the ordinance sets no amount. The EUR 500,000 bank deposit mentioned in the programme note is a practice reported by officials and media, not a recorded rule.

Price at closure (1 Sep 2020; moratorium on new applications from summer 2019): EUR 100,000 contribution to the Public Investment Fund for Sustainable Development, from a press summary; the regulation HG 786/2017 was not read and CJI describes the minimum as EUR 250,000. Strategic-sector investment route EUR 250,000 (t-809faa7c5e).
Set in days of minimum wage (20,000 days of the Mexico City general minimum wage), not in a fixed currency amount, and the current rules were not confirmed.
Fee on the books when the passport-sale clause was repealed (18 Oct 2001), as cut in 1989 from $200,000; printed only as "$". Later amendments may have changed it and were not read.

EUR 200,000 per person in a private investment fund, held 2 years (from 14 Dec 2019). Direct investment route EUR 400,000 plus 10 jobs (t-f29e478627). Discretionary Government decision; a June 2026 draft would remove fixed amounts.

Lowest purchase price: EUR 220,000 in Gozo or the south of Malta; EUR 275,000 elsewhere in Malta (t-1c19c07cc4). Renting instead (EUR 8,750/9,600 a year) is allowed. A tax status, not an immigration permit; minimum tax EUR 15,000 a year. Applies to applications up to 31 Dec 2026; from 2027 the Individual Tax Programme needs EUR 700,000 (t-8a6bce70f6).
Price at closure (30 Jun 2013): property bought for at least EUR 400,000; leasing at EUR 20,000 a year was an alternative. Minimum tax EUR 25,000 a year.

At closure (31 Jul 2020) all three were required together: EUR 650,000 contribution (includes a EUR 10,000 non-refundable deposit), EUR 150,000 in stocks/bonds held 5 years, and a home bought for at least EUR 350,000 held 5 years. Renting at EUR 16,000 a year for 5 years (t-1d63d4db9e) could replace the purchase, in which case the money invested or donated is EUR 800,000.

At closure (Act XXI of 2025, 24 Jul 2025): EUR 600,000 contribution after 36 months' residence (EUR 750,000 after 12 months, t-db49859676), EUR 10,000 donation to an NGO, and a home bought for at least EUR 700,000 held 5 years. Renting at EUR 16,000 a year (t-ab38b2cdd0) could replace the purchase, in which case the money donated is EUR 610,000.

Purchase route: home of at least EUR 375,000 (Malta or Gozo, from 1 Jan 2025) plus EUR 37,000 government contribution (from 22 Jul 2025). Renting at EUR 14,000 a year (t-0165e1528d) replaces the purchase, leaving EUR 37,000 contribution plus rent. Excludes the EUR 60,000 administration fee (t-45af9b2823); applicants must also hold EUR 500,000 in assets (proof, not payment). The 2021 rules also required a EUR 2,000 NGO donation; not checked for 2025.

At closure (29 Mar 2021): EUR 30,000 contribution (of which EUR 5,500 is paid up front as a non-refundable administrative fee; excluding it gives EUR 544,500), EUR 250,000 qualifying investment (government stocks) and a home bought for at least EUR 270,000 in Gozo or the south of Malta (EUR 320,000 elsewhere, t-17631e09cc, making EUR 600,000). Renting (EUR 10,000/12,000 a year) could replace the purchase.

At closure (31 Dec 2022): EUR 250,000 in a listed development project in the north or centre, plus EUR 100,000 to the fund for less developed municipalities, plus EUR 100,000 to the Innovation Fund (added from 31 Dec 2021). In Podgorica or on the coast the project minimum was EUR 450,000 (t-cf43bc8c78), i.e. EUR 650,000 in total. Fees of EUR 15,000 excluded.

Non-refundable contribution to the COVID-19 Projects Development Fund; covers the whole family unit. The criteria are absent from the EDB Act schedule as consolidated to 13 Aug 2026, so whether the route is still open is uncertain.

Not a priced programme: an investment of at least US$500,000 (1999 amendment) lets the Minister, at discretion, accept 2 years' residence instead of the normal requirement. Whether still in force, or whether another sum was prescribed, was not established.
From 13 Aug 2026 the only investor option: US$100,000 initial investment in a business with turnover targets. The US$50,000 option (t-a491f63889) ended then.
Residential property under the IRS/RES/IHS/PDS/Smart City schemes or a G+2 apartment, at least US$375,000. Buyers over 50 can use senior-living PDS property above US$200,000 (t-ba6043def5).
No investment required: the permit rests on transferring income (US$2,000 a month or US$24,000 a year, t-9b14eddf33), not on investing or donating.

Not set because the Silver tier (cheapest standard tier, from June 2024) needs two items in different currencies: a US$150,000 fixed deposit (t-7ed6899447) plus a compulsory home purchase of at least RM600,000 (t-b3249beabf). The Special Economic Zone category needs only US$65,000 (US$32,000 aged 50+) but requires a Forest City home whose minimum price is not recorded.
RM1m fixed deposit (half withdrawable after a year); RM200,000 participation fee excluded. Industry source only, and the programme's current status is not confirmed.
Price at closure (17 Apr 2024): EUR 1,250,000 invested in an innovative Dutch company or SEED fund.
No program_terms rows: the 1997 Act left the amount to Cabinet and no Cabinet determination was found.

Temporary 'Iruwa Initiative' discount for the main applicant, valid to 31 Dec 2026. The standard contribution is US$115,000 (t-0147dd025b, from 29 Jan 2026). Application, due diligence and Program Office fees excluded.

Growth category since 1 April 2025: at least NZ$5 million in managed funds or direct investments approved by Invest New Zealand, held 3 years. Balanced category needs NZ$10 million (t-2e35e2757f). Application fee and levy excluded.
Closed to new applications 27 July 2022; NZ$10 million for three years was the amount on that day, unchanged since 2009.
Closed 27 July 2022; NZ$3 million minimum (four years) since 22 May 2017. Points-based, so the minimum alone did not guarantee an invitation.

10-Year Golden Residency launched 31 Aug 2025: single OMR 200,000 threshold across seven routes (property, company, bonds, shares, deposit...), family included. Source is Invest Oman's page; the legal instrument was not found, and whether the older OMR 250,000 five-year category (t-7ae298c102) survives is unknown.

Since 7 Aug 2021: property of at least B/.200,000 or a three-year fixed deposit of B/.200,000 (same amount). Not purely an investment programme: nationals of listed countries can qualify instead with a job and work permit (t-620fe3da7b), with no investment. B/. at par with USD.

B/.160,000 share capital per applicant under DE 320 of 2008; later amendments and current status not checked (programme status is empty and the category disappears from SNM tables after 2021), so treat as the last known amount.

Under DE 17 of 2026 (from 16 Sept 2026): B/.300,000 for a first-sale (new) property or a presale contract; secondary-market property needs B/.500,000 (t-08807a143d), securities B/.500,000, deposits B/.750,000 (B/.500,000 at state banks). Fees and repatriation deposit excluded.
B/.300,000 in property, a three-year deposit, or a mix (DE 320 of 2008). Amendments after 2008 were not checked.
US$75,000 in a listed company, IPP project or manufacturing/services; spouse and children under 21 included at the same amount. Validity dates not given in the source.

Refundable visa deposit, not a spend. Lowest general amount under the August 2025 Expanded SRRV is US$15,000 for a retiree aged 50+ with a pension (US$800/month); without a pension US$30,000 (t-c53daef1de); aged 40-49 US$25,000/50,000. The Courtesy deposit of US$1,500 (t-1d9dbb7c12) is only for retired diplomats and similar, so not the main route.
No price: ministerial discretion with no amount in law.

Main route today: EUR 500,000 in units of non-real-estate Portuguese investment funds (Law 56/2023, from 7 Oct 2023), the route most applicants now use since real estate and capital transfer were removed. Research and job-creating company routes are also EUR 500,000 (t-d3f6b6811b, t-5ccea19610). The cheapest money route is EUR 250,000 for arts production or cultural heritage (t-0963153d54), up to 20% less in low-density areas; it is a niche donation route, so it is not used as the headline (same choice as Greece, where the EUR 250,000 conversion/listed-building routes are niche). Permit fees (EUR 8,418.90 in 2026) excluded.
Not an investment programme (residence-based card, max 100 a year); no price exists.

Property worth QAR 730,000 in designated areas gives residence while owned; QAR 3,650,000 adds permanent-residency benefits (t-7645b3885d). One source says 'more than' 730,000. Cabinet Decision 28/2020 text not stored.

The scheme's signature product is bought, not invested: a one-time SAR 800,000 payment for permanent premium residency (no investment required); treated here as the price because it is the payment that buys the status, not an add-on fee. Cheaper alternatives: fixed-term residency at SAR 100,000 a year (t-0bd17b63ec); entrepreneur product SAR 400,000 (t-d73d302300, needs a startup and endorsement). Investment products since 2024: property SAR 4 million (t-d664e88ec1), business SAR 7 million plus 10 jobs. Sources are press reports from 2019; current fee not verified.
Closed 15 Apr 2012; investment terms not found in any source read, no term rows.

Option A since 15 Mar 2023: S$10 million in a new or existing business. Option B is S$25 million in a GIP-select fund; Option C a family office with S$200 million AUM and S$50 million deployed. Applicants must also pass business track-record tests (e.g. S$200m turnover).
Non-refundable contribution to the National Transformation Fund, single applicant (Decree-Law 07/2025); USD 95,000 for a family of 2-4. Due diligence USD 5,000 and document fees excluded.
Only the permit fee (SCR 150,000) is recorded; no official minimum property price found.
USD 1 million in a Seychelles business, but also 11 years' aggregate residence, an exam and sponsors: not a quick citizenship route.
USD 1 million (or rupee equivalent) in a Seychelles business plus one year's residence. Permit fee SCR 150,000 excluded.
US$500,000 in a home or business on Providenciales or West Caicos (standard). On Grand Turk and the family islands US$250,000 (in the same row's notes, reg 24(4)(a)(ii); no separate term row).

US$1 million in a home (or home/business) on Providenciales and other main islands. Regional discount: US$300,000 for a home on Grand Turk and family islands (t-dc88f33503). Certificate fee US$25,000 excluded.
US$500,000 in Thai government bonds, companies or property, plus US$1 million in assets (which may include it; t-71c5501c54). Amount as published 2025-26; whether the same at launch not checked.
A non-refundable membership fee, not an investment; it is what buys the long-stay visa, so it is the price. Bronze (5 years) THB 650,000; Gold THB 900,000 (t-fe90282c4d).
Press report (NYT 1992): '$20,000' for a single applicant, $35,000 family of four; currency not stated. Dates of this price and of closure not known.
USD 400,000 in built property (since 13 June 2022; only built/condominium units since 12 Dec 2023), held 3 years. Deposit, bonds, funds, capital and pension routes are USD 500,000.
More than NT$15 million in a profitable business with jobs for 5 nationals for 3 years; bonds route NT$30 million. Start date of the route not established.
Only for Hong Kong and Macao residents: NT$6 million or more, approved by the authority.
Tax residence, not an immigration permit: real estate over 3,500,000 UI (inflation-indexed units) bought from 1 July 2020, plus 60 days' presence a year.

USD 800,000 in a targeted employment area or infrastructure project (most investors use it); standard amount USD 1,050,000 (t-d0d0ff4593). Automatic inflation adjustment due for petitions from 1 Jan 2027, amount not yet published.
USD 1 million unrestricted gift by an individual (each family member needs their own gift per trumpcard.gov); USD 15,000 I-140G fee per person excluded.
Closed April 2001 with no passports issued; no prices recorded.
1990s passport sales: no terms found.
Umbrella id for figures covering several schemes; see vut-dsp, vut-vcp, vut-ciip.

Citizenship Office lists USD 260,000 as the 'Citizenship Fee' for applicant, spouse and one child (a single applicant pays the same).
